newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open lower.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open lower.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were expected to open lower Wednesday.

Gold was likely to soon test the 12-year low of $314.00 an ounce set in early July, as the dollar climbed to a fresh seven-year high overnight on its trade-weighted index and platinum group metals (PGMs) are likely to see a sharp downward correction, after a reversal on TOCOM overnight, led by selling by a U.S. based refiner.
COMEX December gold was called down $1.00 to $2.00 from Tuesday's close of $324.60 after trading from $324.80 to $321.50 on ACCESS.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted early at $318.60/90 compared to the London morning fix of $318.85 and the New York close Tuesday of $320.20/70.

COMEX gold stocks rose a further 15,181 ounces to 944,791 ounces Tuesday, while COMEX silver stocks fell 9,797 ounces to 169,676,386 ounces, after seeing their lowest levels since January earlier this week.
COMEX September silver was called unchanged to down 0.30 cent from Tuesday's close of $4.315.
NYMEX October platinum was expected to open down $5.00 to $10.00 from the previous close at $449.60, after seeing a new contract high Tuesday.
NYMEX September palladium was called down the same from Tuesday's finish of $227.60 after three days of limit-up moves took the contract to new contract highs.
After several days of limit-up moves in TOCOM platinum group metals overnight, PGMs in Tokyo saw a sharp fall overnight, led by heavy selling reported to be by U.S. based refiner Engelhard.
Last month Engelhard had also been reported as a heavy buyer of PGMS on TOCOM.
